text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says after heading Saturday's cabinet meeting that Jordan will continue with economic reforms in a way that will not harm anyone. Says parliamentary elections, scheduled to be held by November, will be held on time and only minimal changes will be made to the election law.

- Higher Council for Investments agrees to the establishment of export companies free from income tax in a bid to encourage exports. The move would extend tax exemption which currently granted only to the producers rather than exporters.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali to visit Qatar on Saturday.
- Geologist says one of Jordan's top nature reservers at Wadi Dana has copper reserves which could earn around 60 million dinars ($90 million) a year over 10 years if exploited.
- Sources say investigation into shooting of seven Israeli schoolgirls last month has been completed. Military court has been set up and soldier Ahmed al-Daqamseh likely to go on trial by mid-May.

- Islamic Action Front secretary general Ishaq al-Farhan says his party and Jordanian opposition in general have been isolated by successive governments which have overlooked the opposition particularly on relations with Israel.

- Munib al-Masri, one of three businessmen organising multi-million dollar fund for Arab investment in Jerusalem, says the group suggested to King Hassan of Morocco a one-off contribution by Arab and Islamic governments of one percent of their annual budget to support Jerusalem.
- Farmers say they are not happy with government compensation for frost in Jordan Valley which cost them seven million dinars.

- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says government is trying to attract the best qualified people into state service. Says no truth in the reported numbers of employees who could be pensioned off.
